audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow adjustments may leak minority-owned earnings into parent owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified net; the computed 28% minority share of 2025 European depreciation and amortization alone is $5.179 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated depreciation, capital expenditure, working-capital changes, and other cash-flow adjustments are combined with income attributable only to IPAR shareholders, creating a numerator-and-share-denominator mismatch.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its subsidiaries, including 72 % owned Interparfums SA, a subsidiary whose stock is publicly traded in France.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-coherence error if the stated owner-earnings construction used consolidated adjustments without allocating Interparfums SA amounts. Depreciation over-addbacks overstate owner earnings, while unallocated capital expenditure or adverse working-capital deductions understate it, so the net direction cannot be established. Because European operations produce about 68% of sales and the affected adjustments recur throughout the owner-earnings history, the error is reasonably capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each historical owner-earnings adjustment by entity, apply 72% to Interparfums SA and 100% to wholly owned operations, then rerun the anchor, trend, and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may give IPAR shareholders cash economically belonging to the subsidiary minority
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum minority correction of $59.177 million, or $1.84 per diluted share, computed as 28% of the entire $211.346 million bridge balance
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash and short-term investments to parent equity without deducting the portion attributable to Interparfums SA's public minority shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 , we had $ 295.2 million in cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments, most of which are held in euro by our European based operations and is readily convertible into U.S. dollars.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim mismatch is demonstrated if the bridge balance is wholly consolidated and unallocated. Nevertheless, even the conservative maximum assumption that all $211.346 million belongs to Interparfums SA limits the error to $1.84 per share, only 2.1%-2.8% of the reported scenario values. Correcting it cannot close the $29.22 gap between the $87.47 bull value and the $116.69 market price or otherwise reverse the valuation conclusion. Distribution restrictions affecting more than the minority allocation would require separate evidence.
audit_findings.action: Trace June 30, 2026 cash and short-term investments by legal entity and correct the bridge for the actual 28% minority claim; separately document any restricted or operationally required cash.

audit_findings.title: Terminal value assumes continuity of earnings generated under finite third-party licenses
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; terminal value is 47.7%-51.5% of scenario value, while the seven largest licensed brands represented 77% of FY2025 sales and brands representing 51% of sales had stated expirations in 2030-2031
audit_findings.mechanism: The growth and terminal-value forecast perpetuates licensed-brand owner earnings beyond contractual expiration dates without explicit renewal, loss, repricing, or replacement economics.
audit_findings.evidence: Substantially all of our prestige fragrance brands are licensed from unaffiliated third parties, and our business is dependent upon the continuation and renewal of such licenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The finite license terms are demonstrated, while actual renewals and their economics remain uncertain. The exposure is material because several major licenses expire before the modeled terminal period and roughly half of modeled value is terminal value. Continuing current earnings indefinitely can overstate value if licenses are lost, renewed on worse terms, or require replacement investment.
audit_findings.action: Build brand-level renewal, loss, and replacement cases using each license expiration, brand sales and owner earnings, renewal terms, entry fees, advertising commitments, inventory runoff, and launch investment; rerun every scenario and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 advertising expense is below management's stated sustainable level
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.862 million pre-tax annual spending gap, computed as 1.2% of $1,488.509 million FY2025 sales; precise parent owner-earnings effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 owner-earnings anchor reflects promotion and advertising at 19.8% of sales, while the forecast compounds that anchor without explicitly normalizing expenditure to management's approximately 21% long-term level.
audit_findings.evidence: Long-term, we continue to anticipate that on a full year basis, promotion and advertising expenditures should aggregate approximately 21% of net sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The 1.2-percentage-point gap is demonstrated and equals 11.4% of the $157.2 million owner-earnings anchor before tax and minority allocation. Although additional advertising may support revenue, omitting the associated recurring cost can materially overstate normalized owner earnings and every scenario derived from it. First-half 2026 advertising remained 18.8% of sales, but management still expected the full year to approach 21%.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the anchor for a 21% advertising ratio with entity-level tax and minority allocation, incorporate identified launch spending, and rerun all scenarios; separately test any revenue benefit attributed to the higher spending.

audit_findings.title: The Lanvin repurchase option creates a discrete 2027 break in the modeled earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: contractual proceeds of approximately $82.3 million gross, or $59.256 million and $1.84 per diluted IPAR share at a 72% economic interest; post-2027 earnings loss is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Exercise would add 2027 sale proceeds but remove subsequent Lanvin owner earnings, whereas nonexercise would preserve the earnings stream without the proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the acquisition of the Lanvin brand names and trademarks for our class of trade, we granted the seller the right to repurchase the brand names and trademarks on July 1, 2027 for € 70 million (approximately $82 million) in accordance with an amendment signed in 2021 .
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual option and exercise price are demonstrated, but the record does not establish exercise likelihood or Lanvin's owner-earnings contribution. The proceeds alone are limited, while the unknown value of earnings removed could be larger. The current valuation does not visibly add the proceeds, so double counting is not demonstrated; the unresolved problem is the absence of mutually exclusive exercise and nonexercise cases.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Lanvin revenue, margins, maintenance investment, tax basis, ownership location, and management's assessment of exercise likelihood; rerun separate continued-ownership and 2027-sale cases without combining their benefits.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter overlooks brands becoming operational after the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 anchor excludes post-anchor revenue, development expense, advertising, royalties, working capital, and launch investment from Goutal, Off-White, Longchamp, and other scheduled additions, while growth is applied with no explicit perimeter reconciliation.
audit_findings.evidence: Amorepacific Europe continued to operate the Goutal brand under an existing license agreement that expired on December 31, 2025, and Interparfums SA began commercial use of the fragrance brand on January 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter change is demonstrated: Goutal commercial operations began January 1, 2026, and Off-White and Longchamp were under development for 2027 launches. The value effect cannot be established because filed information does not isolate their incremental owner earnings. Startup costs could reduce near-term value, while successful proprietary-brand and license economics could increase it.
audit_findings.action: Bridge FY2025 owner earnings to the September 2026 operating perimeter using 2026 actual results by brand or entity, committed launch spending, royalties, working capital, and expected revenue; then rerun scenarios with explicit launch and mature-state economics.
